patients.summary: High school history teacher with Stage II pulmonary sarcoidosis on long-term prednisone, prior sarcoid anterior uveitis, steroid osteopenia and adrenal suppression, and symptomatic fibroids. A 2025 abdominal hysterectomy brings an adrenal crisis, hemorrhage with transfusion, prerenal AKI and a stented left ureteral injury, all settled by early 2026.

Teaches history at the regional high school, asked for a late afternoon slot. Sees outside lung and eye specialists for sarcoidosis, takes prednisone. Booked new patient physical 9/12 at 3:30. Sent the intake packet and records release by email.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 41F, transferring care; prior records requested.

Sarcoidosis: diagnosed in 2022 after an episode of anterior uveitis, workup at that point showed lung involvement, staged II by her pulmonologist. On prednisone 10 mg every day since 2022. Breathing is fine right now, walks most evenings, no cough to speak of. Sees pulmonology about twice a year.
Eyes: one bout of uveitis, red painful eye, treated by ophthalmology, quiet since. Gets slit-lamp exams and eye pressure checks there periodically, last spring, told all fine.
Bones: told she has osteopenia on a bone density scan from the steroids. Takes alendronate weekly and calcium with D twice a day. Tolerating alendronate, no heartburn.
Adrenal: prior doctor told her that after this long on prednisone her own adrenal glands are suppressed and not to stop the prednisone abruptly. Understands that.
Gyn: has fibroids, known for a couple of years. Periods heavy and long, some pelvic pressure. Manages with pads and planning. Not interested in procedures right now. Mom had the same and ended up with a hysterectomy at 45.

Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily; calcium carbonate/D3 600 mg/400 IU BID; alendronate 70 mg weekly.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother fibroids, hysterectomy at 45. Maternal aunt with lupus. Father type 2 diabetes. No one in the family with sarcoid or lung disease.
Social: teaches high school history. Never smoked. Glass of wine a month or two, if that. Lives in Williamsburg.
Prevention: Tdap within the last 10 years per her, prior office to send. Last Pap more than 3 years ago. One mammogram at 40, normal.

Exam: vitals as recorded, BMI about 26. Well appearing. Eyes: conjunctivae clear, pupils equal. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Lungs clear, no crackles, normal effort. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, uterus not palpable above the pelvis. Skin without rash or nodules. No edema. Breast exam without masses. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap with HPV collected; uterus enlarged and irregular on bimanual, nontender, adnexa without masses.

A/P
1. Pulmonary sarcoidosis, Stage II, on chronic prednisone. Stable by her report. Continue per pulmonology; will ask for their notes.
2. Prior sarcoid anterior uveitis. Quiet. Ophthalmology follows.
3. Glucocorticoid-induced adrenal suppression. Do not stop prednisone abruptly; we discussed that illness or surgery would need extra steroid coverage.
4. Osteopenia on steroids. Continue alendronate, calcium/D. Vitamin D level today.
5. Fibroids, symptomatic but tolerable. Revisit if bleeding worsens.
6. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c (steroids), vitamin D, one-time hep C and HIV. Pap/HPV done. Screening mammogram ordered. Flu, COVID and pneumococcal (PCV20, on immunosuppression) at a nurse visit next month. Zoster series in the spring.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ms. Owusu, all of your blood work came back normal, including blood sugar and A1c, kidney and liver tests, blood counts and cholesterol. Vitamin D is in a good range on your supplement. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Your Pap was normal and HPV negative, so no repeat for 5 years. The mammogram order is in; radiology will call you to schedule.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after school for vaccines per PCP. Afebrile, feeling well, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Updated COVID 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. PCV20 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, separate site. Lots and VIS documented. Waited 15 min, no reaction. Told her the arms may ache tomorrow.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. Comparison: outside study from 2022, reported normal. Breast density: heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion in either breast. Axillae unremarkable.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6 month check on long-term prednisone.
Saw pulmonology in January, she says they were happy, same dose. Eye doctor in December, quiet. Breathing ok, no cough. Sleeping fine, appetite stable, no thirst or frequent urination. Periods still heavy, a heavy day or two where she plans around class, no dizziness. Taking alendronate correctly on Sunday mornings.
Records from prior office arrived and were reviewed: Tdap 2019, bone density in 2022 read as osteopenia, consistent with what she told me.

Exam: BP and weight stable. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. Skin clear on shins and arms.

A/P
Sarcoidosis on prednisone 10 mg: unchanged, per pulm.
Steroid monitoring: BMP and A1c today.
Osteopenia: continue current regimen.
Fibroids: tolerable, she will message if worse.
Shingrix #1 today (immunosuppressed on prednisone); #2 in 2 to 6 months, RN visit.
Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sugar, A1c, potassium and kidney numbers all normal. Nothing to change. Book the second shingles shot for May.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. After dose 1 she had only some arm soreness. Series now complete. Observed without issue.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 42F.
Interval: good year. Pulmonology visit in July, she reports stable and no dose change. Eyes checked in the spring, fine. No cough, no shortness of breath climbing the stairs at school. Fibroid bleeding the same, heavy for a couple of days a month. Mood good, sleeping ok. Exercise: walking, some yard work.
Meds: prednisone 10 daily, calcium/D BID, alendronate weekly. NKDA.

ROS otherwise negative: no fevers, no weight change, no vision changes, no joint pain, no bowel or urinary change.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Eyes clear. Oropharynx normal. No lymphadenopathy. Thyroid not enlarged. Lungs clear throughout. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: no nodules or plaques. Extremities without edema.

A/P
1. Sarcoidosis, pulmonary Stage II and prior uveitis: stable on prednisone 10, specialists following.
2. Steroid effects: CMP, A1c, lipids, vitamin D today. Osteopenia on alendronate.
3. Adrenal suppression: reviewed again that she needs extra steroid if she gets sick or has any procedure; she should tell any surgeon.
4. Fibroids: unchanged; CBC today.
5. Prevention: flu and COVID given today. Mammogram ordered. Pap current. PHQ-2 negative.
Follow-up in 6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything normal again: blood count, sugar and A1c, kidney, liver, cholesterol, vitamin D. Even with the heavy periods your blood count is fine. Talk soon.

reports.text: Bilateral digital breast tomosynthesis, standard views. Compared with 11/2023. Heterogeneously dense tissue. No new mass, suspicious calcifications or distortion. Skin and nipples unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Repeat in one year.
